In clinical practice and radiology exams, the presence of right paratracheal adenopathy alongside BHL is extremely common in sarcoidosis (Garland's triad / 1-2-3 sign). Even if present, if there are no pulmonary infiltrates, it is often still grouped into early stage or Stage I in some simplified contexts, OR the question implies that the *findings shown* represent the diagnosis of Stage I (implying the paratracheal nodes might be considered part of the nodal stage rather than parenchymal).
Actually, the Scadding staging for Stage I is strictly "bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy". Parenchymal involvement makes it Stage II. Paratracheal nodes are *nodal*, not parenchymal. So BHL + Paratracheal is still technically Stage I (nodal only), whereas BHL + Lung opacities is Stage II.
Therefore, since the image shows BHL and paratracheal widening but *clear lungs* (no opacities), it fits Stage I (nodal disease only). Option C says "with paratracheal", which matches the image and fits the "nodal only" criteria for Stage I.
